composition.serve_who: This is a BUILDING/STRUCTURAL GA (positions, dimensions, structural details — perspective, plan, sections, details, dimension tables — no flow/loop connectivity of a control system). It serves the twin rudder/steering system: rudder blades (port + stbd, mirrored), their bearing structures, the central sheave/car linkage that mechanically couples the two rudder arms to the wheel-driven track, and the autopilot ram/rod support. Evidence: title block "Steering System GA" 108-01-150-001; leaders naming "UPPER/LOWER BEARING STRUCTURE", "TRI-BEAM 11", "PARTITION LM1/LM2", "BHD L", "AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT ... BOLTED THROUGH BHD L", rudder blade sections, and the toe-in/Ackermann tables and safety notes describing the 3-independent-path (2 wheels + pilot) steering redundancy. The mechanical structure (bearing housings, sheaves, tri-beams, partitions, track/car) is shared infrastructure supporting both rudder blades and the autopilot ram — captured under infrastructure, not duplicated per rudder.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet shows twin rudder stocks/blades, mirrored port/stbd about CL, each with its own bearing structure, arm, and rod link to the central car — matches established node 150-rudder-blades which already carries toe-in/Ackermann/redundancy facts from this same drawing.

functions.label: Independent rudder actuation via steering cylinder + rudder arm
functions.sheet_region: Perspective view (top-left), Plan view (center-right), Section C-C (bottom-left)
functions.what_it_does: Each rudder stock is turned by its own steering cylinder acting on a rudder arm; a rod link from the arm connects to the central movable car so both rudders move together while each stock/arm/cylinder set stays mechanically independent (no cross-linkage line drawn between the two arms except via the shared car).
key_components: Rudder stock — port and starboard, mirrored
Rudder arm — one per stock, drives/receives rod link
Steering cylinder — one per rudder stock
Rod link (2044mm nominal at neutral) — arm-to-car connection
Upper bearing structure (ref DWG 108-05-151-001) — top rudder bearing/housing
Lower bearing structure (ref DWG 108-05-151-002) — bottom rudder bearing/housing
Water-tight system neoprene tube (item 6, D=305mm) — hull penetration seal
functions.dry_data: Rod link 2044mm long at neutral gives 1.8° toe-in; toe-in variation table 2025-2056mm rod length -> 0-3° toe-in. Rudder BOM: 180mm/220mm aluminium sheaves, GRP bearing housings, GRP rudder assembly (item 18, ~107.5kg/215kg total mass for 2).

functions.label: Steering position sensing/coordination for autopilot per Ackermann table
functions.what_it_does: Defines the geometric relationship between the central car's position and each rudder's angle (inside vs outside rudder), so the rudder set produces correct differential (Ackermann) steering as the car/track moves off centerline.
key_components: Rod links from each rudder arm
functions.dry_data: Car position 0/98/212/316.5/364.3mm from CL -> inside rudder angle 1.8/10/20/30/35°, outside rudder angle -1.8/6.3/16.0/25.3/30.0°. Car race ±365mm from CL.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: A distinct pilot rod/ram is called out separately from the two wheel-driven rudder linkages: 'AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT IS BOLTED THROUGH BHD L' and 'MAKE PENETRATION IN TRI-BEAM TO SUIT PILOT ROD MOVEMENT' are unique callouts naming the autopilot path, distinct from the wheel/car/sheave mechanism used by the two wheels.

functions.label: Autopilot ram drives rudder linkage independently of the wheel/cable path
functions.sheet_region: Section B-B / plan view center, callouts 'AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT...' and 'MAKE PENETRATION IN TRI-BEAM...'
functions.what_it_does: An autopilot ram, structurally supported by bolting through Bulkhead L (with tapping plates bonded on the fwd face), pushes/pulls a pilot rod that passes through a purpose-made penetration in Tri-beam 11 to move the rudder linkage — providing the third of the three independent steering paths (2 wheels + pilot) per the safety notes.
key_components: BHD L — structural support point, bolted through with bonded tapping plates on fwd face
Tri-beam 11 — penetrated to allow pilot rod travel
functions.dry_data: Autopilot ram: 300mm stroke, metal, qty 1, ~40kg total mass (item 19 BOM).

facts: Central track/car (item 13, ASSEMBLED CAR CAR190) rides on a 1100mm track (item 11, JP3, GRP) mounted on centerline; car race travel is ±365mm from CL.

Wire ropes/Vectran line (item 14, 20mm) run from the central car outboard to port and stbd lower sheave boxes, passing around 180mm/220mm aluminium sheaves (items 1 supported by items 2-5 bearing housings) — mechanically coordinates both rudders from wheel input while each rudder retains its independent arm/cylinder.
Upper sheave box (item 8, LAM/FRP) and lower sheave box (item 9, LAM-108-01-150-004 & 108-01-150-006, FRP) house the sheave/cable interface — see Detail A and Port Lower Sheave Box Detail.
Sheave boxes to be bonded horizontally per note 'BOND SHEAVE BOXES HORIZONTALLY' (plan view, right side).

E-glass wedge stops (item 12) limit travel; rod-link carbon tube + end fittings + M16 ball joints (item 15) connect car to rudder arms (item 16/17, port/stbd, filler-arm assemblies with autopilot connector, ~40kg each).
Track support uses a 16mm tapping plate insert per Detail E, ref DWG 108-01-150-004.

Structural mounting: upper bearing structure ref DWG 108-05-151-001; lower bearing structure ref DWG 108-05-151-002; longitudinal Tri-beam 11 (both port and stbd, i.e. items 6 & 7 per beam callout 'TRI-BEAM 11, 6, 7'); transverse Partitions LM1 (port) and LM2 (stbd) support the mid structure; hull shell is the outer boundary with G10 spacers (30mm) isolating rudder tube penetrations (Section B-B).
Datum 0 / DWL (design waterline) reference lines used for vertical positioning of bearings/sheave boxes (Section C-C, Section B-B).
